neighbours.label: the word right after a form of 'go' in a fixed idiom (gone the same way, went the extra mile, go the distance)
fire: Video rental stores have gone the way of the telegraph in most towns.
The nurses went the extra mile to keep the patients comfortable.
Few boxers expected the young challenger to go the distance.
Last year's festival was rained out, and this one may go the same way.
When they renovated the kitchen, they decided to go the whole hog.
Plenty of famous restaurants have gone the way of their founders.
The volunteers always go the extra step to welcome new families.
Many old factories in the valley have gone the same way as the mill.
quiet: Video rental stores have mostly closed down in most towns.
The nurses worked long shifts to keep the patients comfortable.
Few boxers expected the young challenger to survive the fight.
Last year's festival was rained out, and this one may be cancelled too.
When they renovated the kitchen, they decided to replace everything.
Plenty of famous restaurants have closed after their founders retired.
The volunteers always make an effort to welcome new families.
Many old factories in the valley were shut down just like the mill.

notes: Probe: 'gone the same way' 0.92, 'went the extra mile' 0.74, 'going in for' 0.32, 'go for the' 0.29, Spanish 'llevarán a cabo' 0.36; same sentences without go 0.004-0.007.
